notes_list.title: Free Radicals
notes_list.basic_overview: Organic radicals are species with an unpaired electron. Their stability is affected by resonance, hyperconjugation and substitution, while radical reactions often proceed through chain processes.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Benzylic and allylic radicals are strongly stabilized by resonance. Tertiary radicals are usually more stable than secondary and primary alkyl radicals.
notes_list.examples: NBS/hν allylic bromination; peroxide-initiated additions illustrate radical chain chemistry.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Light, heat or radical initiators can start chains. Oxygen may inhibit radical reactions by trapping radicals.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Initiation creates radicals. 2. Propagation consumes one radical and generates another. 3. Termination removes radicals. 4. Track regioselectivity and resonance of radical intermediates.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Chain kinetics can show non-simple orders because initiation, propagation and termination determine steady-state radical concentration.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Useful for allylic/benzylic halogenation and polymerization concepts.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not draw ionic curved arrows for radical steps; use single-headed fishhook arrows conceptually.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
